sentences.text: Protosuchus had short jaws that broadened at the skull base to provide a large attachment surface for jaw muscles. It possessed dentition resembling modern crocodiles, with lower jaw teeth fitting into notches on the upper jaw.
This quadrupedal reptile walked on columnar legs where the rear limbs were longer than the front ones.
The animal was about 80 centimeters in length.
It possessed a powerful tail used for propulsion while moving in water.
The genus Protosuchus was described by Brown in 1934.
There are 16 recorded fossil occurrences of Protosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
Protosuchus likely fed on terrestrial animals the size of a lizard.
It lived in rivers and swamps.
Protosuchus belongs to the suborder Protosuchia.
It is classified within the family Protosuchidae.
The genus has been synonymized with Archaeosuchus, Baroqueosuchus, and Lesothosuchus.
Protosuchus fossils date to the Early Jurassic period.
The animal lived approximately 200 to 184 million years ago during the Norian and Rhaetian stages.
Protosuchus existed from the Rhaetian to the Sinemurian, between 205.7 and 192.9 million years ago.
Fossils have been found in what is now North America and possibly South Africa.
Researchers interpreting the holotype of Erythrochampsa longipes suggest it may belong to or be a relative of Protosuchus.
